summary: Mrs. Anna (Maria) Meier of Wilkes-Barre, d. 1897 — lead prosecutrix in the Rockafellow bank case; NOT John's Maria A.; kinship unproven.
bio: A depositor on the bank's last day, she lost $700, fought the embezzlement case of failed banker F. V. Rockafellow (1893–97) to the Superior Court, which reversed a lower-court ruling in 1897, told the judge in open court she 'did not think justice had been done', and died July 1897 after a fall on her way home from friends on Grove Street.
